resolutions.decision: Root selected opt-in persistence, consistent with the existing explicit-capture workflow. ADR discovery now promises JSON metadata on successful discovery, and landing.html/response.json persistence only with --capture-discovery PATH.
resolutions.alternatives: Unconditional persistence would require choosing a default artifact destination and changing ordinary discovery behavior. That expansion was not selected. This revision is an intentional contract clarification, not a mechanical typo or a claim that the old unconditional prose was already satisfied.
resolutions.verification: Public-run default_discovery child case emits discovery JSON and creates neither capture directory nor supplementary artifacts. The explicit discovery case still verifies exact landing bytes and provenance.

resolutions.decision: Complete-response provenance is merged before status/MIME/storage validation. Failed acquisitions retain known requested/final URLs, http_status, MIME, complete byte count/hash and provenance timestamp when available. local_relative_path remains conditional on validated storage.
resolutions.incomplete_response: A private publisher-only error carries known final URL/status/MIME from body failures and the last retryable HTTP response. It carries no complete-body hash/count. Each new fetch records attempted_at; failed acquisitions record failed_at and error. A pre-response failure invents no response fields.
resolutions.alternatives: Success-only documentation was rejected because it would discard known evidence and weaken the intended manifest contract. No generic HTTP error hierarchy, response archive, provider expansion or retry policy change was added.
resolutions.verification: Regression tests cover complete403, MIME rejection, deterministic storage failure, no-response error, redirected truncation, body timeout, and exhausted429 headers. Existing partial acquisition, reuse, corruption detection and main-file preservation remain green.

resolutions.decision: The workflow describes a conditional diagnostic attempt on discovery failure with capture enabled: first absolute anchor accepted by the publisher URL scope and path ending /epub, if prior diagnostics do not abort. Missing XML metadata does not prevent the attempt. EPUB contents are not validated by this capture.
resolutions.verification: Public-run child cases establish that recognized empty sections skip EPUB; relative-only links are ineligible; the first eligible absolute link is used even without XML metadata; and a propagated XML decode error prevents EPUB capture.
